post_text:
I watched a junior lead a meeting I knew I could finish in five minutes.

I stayed silent while they struggled to find the right words.

My hands hovered over the mute button, ready to "save" the conversation.

I wanted to jump in and fix the silence before it became awkward.

But I realized that my intervention would be a theft. 🤐

Every time I solve a problem for someone else, I steal their chance to grow.

The room felt heavy as the client waited for an answer.

The junior took a breath, gathered their thoughts, and delivered a solution I hadn't even considered.

It wasn't the way I would have said it, but it worked better for the audience.

I had to learn that my way is just one way, not the only way.

Stepping back is harder than stepping up.

It requires trusting the process over the immediate result.

By the end of the hour, they walked out taller.

I walked out realizing my job isn't to be the smartest person in the room anymore. 📈
lesson_extracted: True leadership is measured by how much space you leave for others to fill.
